tasks.label: Document classification
tasks.description: Decide what an uploaded document is.
tasks.volumeGuidance: High volume, low complexity — a small local model handles this well.

tasks.label: Document extraction
tasks.description: Pull structured fields out of a document.
tasks.volumeGuidance: High volume; needs reliable structured output.

tasks.label: Billing diagnosis
tasks.description: Diagnose a blocked billing item and propose resolutions.
tasks.volumeGuidance: Low volume, high stakes — this reaches the ledger, so it requires a provider marked trusted.

tasks.label: Scope classification
tasks.description: Decide whether a chat message is about this organization's freight at all.
tasks.volumeGuidance: Runs on every assistant turn and needs only a yes/no — the cheapest thing to route to a small local model.

tasks.label: Assistant chat
tasks.description: Answer questions and drive the tool loop in the assistant.
tasks.volumeGuidance: Interactive and multi-step; needs reliable tool calling and favours a capable model.

tasks.label: Operational insights
tasks.description: Write the explanation on a finding whose numbers were already computed.
tasks.volumeGuidance: A batch every few hours. It never produces a number or a severity, so it is safe to route to whatever is cheapest.

tasks.label: Daily briefing
tasks.description: Write the morning page from figures that were already gathered.
tasks.volumeGuidance: A handful of calls once a day. Like insights it writes only wording, so the cheapest model that writes clean English will do.

tasks.label: Table questions
tasks.description: Turn a sentence into a table's filters and sort.
tasks.volumeGuidance: One short call each time somebody asks a table a question. It names fields from a catalogue it is shown and writes no SQL, and everything it names is compiled against that catalogue afterwards, so a cheap model that guesses wrong produces an unresolved line rather than a wrong answer.

tasks.label: Inbound mail
tasks.description: Decide what an email that arrived on a monitored address is.
tasks.volumeGuidance: One call per message, so it follows how much mail is forwarded. It answers with a label from a fixed set that is re-checked afterwards, so the cheapest model that reads English reliably will do.

tasks.label: Accounting mapping
tasks.description: Choose which accounting-system record matches a Trenova record when the name rules are unsure.
tasks.volumeGuidance: Runs only for records the deterministic matcher could not settle, at most a hundred per refresh and usually a handful. It picks from a supplied list, so a small, inexpensive model is enough.

tasks.label: Evaluation judge
tasks.description: Score a sample of agents' answers to their evaluation cases against each case's rubric.
tasks.volumeGuidance: A few calls a night, only when judging is on in AI Control. Its reading counts toward the evaluation budget and never overrides a check that failed outright, so a capable model that follows a rubric closely is worth more here than a cheap one.

tasks.label: Embedding
tasks.description: Turn memories, documents and mail into vectors so agents can find them by meaning rather than by exact words.
tasks.volumeGuidance: High volume and cheap: every indexed record is embedded once and every search embeds its question. Needs an embedding model, not a chat model, and a fixed dimension; changing the model re-indexes everything.

tasks.label: General
tasks.description: Anything not routed to a more specific task.

embeddingInputStyles.label: Same for documents and queries
embeddingInputStyles.description: Documents and search queries are sent as they are.

embeddingInputStyles.label: Voyage input type
embeddingInputStyles.description: Sends input_type document or query, and the dimension as output_dimension, the way Voyage's API expects.

embeddingInputStyles.label: Nomic prefixes
embeddingInputStyles.description: Prefixes each text with search_document: or search_query:, which nomic-embed-text needs to embed each side of a search correctly.

kinds.label: Anthropic Messages
kinds.description: Anthropic's API, and any endpoint serving the same shape such as Amazon Bedrock.

kinds.label: OpenAI Responses
kinds.description: OpenAI's Responses API, and endpoints serving the same shape.

kinds.label: OpenAI-compatible
kinds.description: Any server exposing /chat/completions — vLLM, SGLang, LM Studio, OpenRouter, Groq, Together, Fireworks, DeepInfra, and others.

kinds.label: Ollama
kinds.description: Ollama's native API. Used instead of its OpenAI-compatible endpoint, which ignores JSON schemas.

presets.label: OpenAI embeddings
presets.notes: Semantic retrieval through OpenAI's embeddings endpoint.

presets.label: Voyage AI embeddings
presets.notes: Retrieval-tuned embeddings. Documents and queries are sent with Voyage's input_type so each is embedded for its side of a search.

presets.label: Gemini embeddings
presets.notes: Gemini's OpenAI-compatible endpoint. The model's native size is reduced to the dimension chosen here.

presets.label: OpenRouter
presets.notes: Routes to hundreds of models across many upstream providers.

presets.label: Groq
presets.notes: Lowest time to first token; useful for high-volume classification.

presets.label: Amazon Bedrock
presets.notes: Use the bedrock-mantle endpoint for your region and a Bedrock API key, for example https://bedrock-mantle.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/openai/v1.

presets.label: Ollama (self-hosted)
presets.notes: Runs open-weight models on your own hardware; no data leaves your network.

presets.label: Ollama embeddings (self-hosted)
presets.notes: Semantic retrieval on your own hardware. nomic-embed-text returns 768 dimensions and expects search_document and search_query prefixes.

presets.label: vLLM (self-hosted)
presets.notes: Enforces JSON schemas server-side; the strongest self-hosted option for throughput.

presets.label: llama.cpp (self-hosted)
presets.notes: llama-server does not reliably honour response_format on its OpenAI-compatible route, so schemas are sent in the prompt instead.
